objective: Run the quarterly knowledge compounding test: pick three old missions whose records carry a measured cost, ask whether today's lab would solve them faster, cheaper or better, and report the delta with its mechanism named rather than assuming a learning rate
rationale: The strategy's line is that the delta IS the learning rate and that it must be measured rather than assumed. The test has never been run and no candidate list exists, yet the lab is unusually well placed to run it because the DAFoam case status record carries mesh size, measured core-minutes and a per-attempt breakdown for every rung, which means the waste is already separated from the useful spend. Three candidates carry that separation cleanly. The MACH tutorial wing at 38,304 cells cost 692.5 core-minutes of which 207.1 were lost to an out-of-memory kill during host contention followed by a host reboot mid-run, so 30 percent of its price was infrastructure failure of exactly the class the launcher and the orphan cure now prevent structurally. The ONERA M6 wing spent about 127.5 core-minutes across three primal attempts and its whole conditioning campaign later turned out to have run under a preconditioner option that is dead code for its solver, which took 214.2 hours to root-cause and is the single longest entry in the time-to-root-cause table; re-run today under the adopted lever echo it would be provably measuring what it claims to measure. The CRM wing-alone case at 579,072 cells lost two of its three attempts to an orphaned and corrupted checkpoint, the failure mode the collector cure addressed structurally. Each therefore comes with a named mechanism for its expected delta rather than a hope. Two honesty constraints belong in the design. The selection rule is fixed before any re-run so the test cannot be gamed, and the rank basis must be pinned first: the per-family cost scaling laws were fitted on ledger rows that all ran at one rank, and most approved compute estimates on the docket state no rank count, so a cross-mission core-minute comparison that skips this compares two different units. Axis A: report-kind, and the re-runs are priced from the missions' own measured spend. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: zero for this pass, which is a selection and design sweep over records already on disk; the re-runs themselves are priced in the follow-on filing this pass produces, each from the measured core-minute figure its own mission record carries, which is the basis class the calibration scorecard found holds to a worst case of 1.84 times against 13.55 times for forecast-priced items
expected_knowledge_gain: A number for the learning rate with its decomposition, and three outcomes that separate. One: the missions come back cheaper and better with the delta attributed to named machinery, which tells the lab which of its instruments actually paid and justifies the next quarter's slow-burn budget. Two: cheaper but not better, or better but not cheaper, which is the trade the lab has been making unmeasured and which changes what the standing discipline is worth. Three: no delta, which would say the compounding is imagined and the machinery is overhead, and that is the most valuable of the three to learn. The pass also produces the rank-basis correction the cost comparison needs, which is worth having on its own.
sequencing: Dispatchable now for the design and selection pass, which spends no solver time. The re-runs it prices are quarterly-review work under strategy rule 5 and queue behind Ladder V under rule 1.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Knowledge compounding test: quarterly, pick 3 old missions; would today's lab solve them faster/cheaper/better? Measure, don't assume. The delta IS the learning rate.' Operationalised: three missions selected by a rule fixed and committed before any re-run, drawn only from missions carrying a measured core-minute figure and a gradeable result; each re-run under current machinery at a pinned rank count matching the original; each reporting measured core-minutes then against now, wall time then against now, and the graded result then against now under the same criterion. The delta is decomposed into cheaper compute, fewer wasted runs and better answer, with the mechanism named for each part. A test that reports a delta without the decomposition, that compares across unpinned rank counts, or that swaps a mission after seeing its re-run, fails.
